records.name: Philadelphia Adult League Softball (PALS)
records.summary: Mixed gender slow pitch softball for adults. Weeknight and Sunday leagues play at a West Philadelphia rec center.
records.what_you_do: Join a team or sign on as a free agent, then play weekly games. Umpires are provided, and each team pays a fee per game for them.

schedule.text: Leagues run Monday, Tuesday and Thursday evenings (6 to 10 pm) and Sunday days (10 am to 5 pm). Two seasons a year, the first starting in spring and the second in July.

locations.label: Tiffany Fletcher Rec Center, formerly Mill Creek Rec Center

cost.text: Teams pay $865 per season plus $20 per game for umpires, paid at the field. Free agents pay $80 per person when a spot is available, plus the same $20 per game. Registrations are not refundable.

requirements.gear: Men use wooden bats only. Women and non-binary players use USA approved bats. Plastic or molded cleats are allowed, and metal cleats are not.

first_step.how: Email kelly@phillypals.com to get on the waitlist, since the summer and fall 2026 seasons are full.
first_step.basis: The current season is full, so the only way in is a waitlist by email, and players must register as a team or as a free agent.
first_step.what_to_expect: Games are on weeknight evenings and Sunday days at the Tiffany Fletcher Rec Center, in two ten-game seasons with a single-elimination playoff. Umpires are provided, and every team is guaranteed at least one playoff game. Teams get 15 shirts and a scorebook when the season begins.
first_visit_tips: Men use wooden softball bats only. Women and non-binary players need USA or ASA approved bats.
Wear plastic or molded cleats, since metal cleats are not allowed.
There is ample free street parking around the rec center.
Teams need four or more women or non-binary players, counting the roster and the field.

records.notes: Site is one page with section links. The league rules are in a Google Doc whose text did not load, so no rule details are recorded. The LeagueApps login was not used. Summer and fall 2026 are sold out. The youth camp in the news has no year and is not used. The homepage names Change Up Sports as a nonprofit with no web address found, so it is not listed as a lead.

records.name: Philadelphia Alliance for Labor Support (PALS)
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives free doula support during labor to people who could not otherwise get it, and offers subsidized doula training.
records.what_you_do: Trained volunteer doulas support families through labor and birth. People who want to become doulas can join the subsidized training waitlist.

schedule.text: Subsidized doula trainings run about twice a year, with a waitlist. The site lists no start dates.

cost.text: Doula support is free for families who could not otherwise get doula care. Training is subsidized, and the site does not say what students pay.

first_step.how: Join the training waitlist through the form on the Become a Doula page. If you already hold a doula training certificate, use the Volunteer with PALS sign-up form instead.
first_step.basis: Volunteers need a doula training certificate before they sign up, and training is limited with a long waitlist, so a newcomer cannot try the work first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer doulas are on call from two weeks before to two weeks after a client's due date, take prenatal clients, and pick up hospital on-call shifts of 6, 8 or 12 hours from a shared calendar. Each client has a consent form, and each birth needs a birth record form afterward.
first_visit_tips: Have a photo of your doula training certificate ready, since the volunteer form asks for one.
A mentorship sign-up form exists for mentors and mentees, and the site calls it optional.
The site strongly encourages a hospital orientation, but does not say it is required.

records.notes: Contact email addresses on the contact page are hidden in the page text, so none is recorded; the contact page is the way to reach them. The site does not state eligibility for training, the cost to students, or any dates, so status stays probably_active. Corrected what_you_do: the subsidized training is for people who want to become doulas.

records.name: Philadelphia GAA (Gaelic Athletic Association)
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the Gaelic Athletic Association. Its site covers Gaelic football, hurling and camogie, and it has a youth page for young players.
records.what_you_do: Play Gaelic football, hurling or camogie with one of the clubs on the Teams page, or sign a young player up through the youth program, which runs through five youth clubs. The group's pages do not describe trial sessions, so ask a club or an officer how to start.

locations.label: Limerick Field Complex, Pottstown, PA (listed as the group's headquarters)

cost.text: No fees are published on the group's site, so ask each club.

first_step.how: Email the group's public relations officer at the address on the Contact Us page to ask which club to try first, or contact a club from the Teams page directly.
first_step.basis: The site lists clubs and officer emails but names no trial or beginner session, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group's pages do not say when or where a team trains, what it costs, or whether beginners can try a session. Each team on the Teams page links to its own club website or Facebook page, so ask that club what a first session looks like.
first_visit_tips: Check the club's own page or Facebook for practice times, since the group's pages do not list them.
Ask whether the club lends equipment to new players, because the group's pages do not say.
For a young player, the youth page names five youth clubs, and each has its own link.

records.notes: Team and youth pages name clubs but give no training times, trial sessions, or fees. The contact page lists one role mailbox per officer; the public relations address is used as the general contact, which is our choice and not a published general line. The 2025 board listing is the newest dated item, so last_sign_of_life is 2025. Hurling and camogie have no exact tag, so football_rugby is the nearest. The Pottstown field is the listed headquarters and may not be where teams train. Clubs named on the pages were not fetched (see leads_only). Several clubs link only to Facebook and have no web address recorded. One search snippet pointed to an adult learn-to-hurl offer by a listed club; that club is a different group and the page was not opened.

records.name: Philadelphia Asian American Film Foundation
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs a yearly film festival and year-round screenings and talks about Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander stories. Volunteers help run the festival and the year-round work.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer for festival shifts or on a year-round staff committee (sponsorship, marketing, programming, guest services or volunteer coordination) through the inquiry form on its site. Or attend a screening or talk.

schedule.text: Screenings and talks run through the year, with a yearly 11-day film festival. Staff volunteers plan the work on year-round committees.

cost.text: Event prices are not listed on the site. Each volunteer shift earns a shirt and one free ticket to a paid event, and food is provided. Donations are welcome.

first_step.how: Send an inquiry through the volunteer form on paaff.org/volunteer, or ask about volunteering at a screening or talk.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says film experience is not required and gives an inquiry form to start, so it explicitly welcomes newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Festival volunteers help with programming and screenings during the 11-day festival, and staff volunteers join committees that plan the work year-round, such as sponsorship, marketing, programming, guest services or volunteer coordination. The site does not say how long a shift runs or how many people it needs, so ask in your inquiry.
first_visit_tips: Say which role you want in your inquiry: a festival shift or a year-round committee.
Ask about shift length before you commit, since the site does not give it.
Each shift earns a volunteer shirt, one free ticket to a paid event, and food.

records.notes: The 2026 festival site loaded only a placeholder, so festival dates and ticket prices are not recorded. Tier 1 days and times came from one-off October events and were cleared from the schedule; the October 11 and October 20 events are kept only as last_sign_of_life. The site gives no accessibility notes, so wheelchair stays unknown.

records.name: Philadelphia Association for Financial Professionals (PAFP)
records.summary: A professional association for treasury, finance and accounting workers in the Philadelphia area. It holds monthly meetings and lunch and learns, plus a learning day and seasonal member events.
records.what_you_do: Attend a monthly meeting or lunch and learn, network with finance professionals, or join as a member.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings and lunch and learns, held both virtually and in person, plus a learning day and seasonal events for members.

cost.text: Membership is $195, or $350 with the Learning Day. Members pay $175 to $195 for the Learning Day alone, and non-members pay $225 to $250. Education, retired and in-transition people pay no fee but volunteer for the association. Events outside a membership level have an extra registration fee.

first_step.how: Register for a lunch and learn through the registration link on the events page, or start a membership application with the Join Now link.
first_step.basis: Events have public registration links and membership is open to individuals, students, and retired or in-transition people, but the site does not say whether non-members can join the monthly meetings.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sessions are educational talks for finance, treasury and accounting people, with time to network. Meetings run both virtually and in person, and members get discounted registration and access to member-only events.
first_visit_tips: Check the registration page for the price before you sign up, because the site does not list event prices.
The session listed on the events page is virtual, so you can attend from home.
The only street address on the site is the Conshohocken office, which is outside the city.

records.notes: The tier 1 summary mentioned a yearly conference, but no conference appears on the site, so it is replaced with the learning day. The site does not say whether non-members can attend monthly meetings, what they cost, or where in-person meetings are held. The Conshohocken office is the only street address found. The registration page redirects to a membership platform and states no format, fees or venue.

records.name: Philadelphia Beekeepers Guild
records.summary: Beekeepers and bee lovers who promote sustainable urban beekeeping through monthly meetings, a shared apiary, and a yearly honey festival.
records.what_you_do: Come to monthly meetings to learn beekeeping, join the group's work at its apiary, and help with the honey festival. Free virtual Bee Chats also run on some first Tuesdays.

schedule.text: Monthly guild meeting on the third Thursday at 7 pm, usually listed as hybrid, plus a free virtual Bee Chat on some first Tuesdays.

cost.text: Events are listed as free. Membership dues run from $15 to $100 a year, with lifetime options of $250 and $500.

first_step.how: Come to the third Thursday guild meeting at St. James School, or join the free virtual Bee Chat on a first Tuesday.
first_step.basis: Meetings and Bee Chats are listed as free and public, with a clear membership page, but the site does not say beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Monthly meetings run from 7 to 9 pm on the third Thursday at St. James School, and many are listed as hybrid so you can join online. Some meetings have a named speaker, and the Bee Chat is a free virtual evening on some first Tuesdays. The classes page listed no events when checked on 2026-10-08, so a beginner class is not scheduled right now.
first_visit_tips: Use the RSVP link on the event listing, since each meeting has one.
Check the listing for whether you can join online, because meetings are listed as hybrid.
Arrive for the 7 pm start, since listings run until 9 pm.

records.notes: The membership page does not say whether visitors can attend meetings before joining, and the apiary visit rules are not stated. Honey Fest news items on the homepage have no dates on the page. The classes page showed no listed events. Contact name carried over from the e-postcard record. Calendar feed is the group's own iCal export of its events list.

records.name: Rittenhouse Sound (Philadelphia Chapter SPEBSQSA)
records.summary: Philadelphia's lower-voice a cappella chorus. Singers rehearse each week, perform in concerts, and take part in chapter quartet contests.
records.what_you_do: Audition year-round to join the chorus and sing at weekly Tuesday rehearsals. Prospective singers can visit a rehearsal first, and the events page lists concerts and showcases.

schedule.text: Weekly rehearsals on Tuesdays, 7:15 to 9:45 pm, at the Philadelphia Ethical Society on Rittenhouse Square. Some 2026 rehearsals moved to other venues, so check the events page before you go.

cost.text: The site does not list dues, audition fees, or visitor fees.

access.notes: An ADA ramp is at the building's rear, addressed 1909 Manning St, and a stair lift serves the main theater floor. The site does not describe access to the second-floor community room used on some second Tuesdays.

first_step.how: Fill in the guest registration form on the Visit page, then come to a Tuesday rehearsal. When you are ready, audition through the Audition page.
first_step.basis: The site invites prospective singers to a rehearsal, says you can audition on a first visit, and says sheet music reading is not required.
first_step.what_to_expect: A rehearsal runs from 7:15 to 9:45 pm on Tuesdays at the Philadelphia Ethical Society, and visitors are invited after they register. The audition has three short parts: singing a memorized section of a provided song on a voice part you choose, singing up to 30 seconds of any song a cappella, and learning a simple barbershop tag with others.
first_visit_tips: Audition materials are in a linked folder, so you can prepare at your own pace.
On the second Tuesday of the month, rehearsal starts in the second-floor community room and moves to the main floor at about 8:15 pm.
Some metered street spots are free after set hours, and many are free after 6:30 pm; evening lots run about $13 to $24.

records.notes: Audition and visit pages give steps; the site publishes no dues or fees. The events page lists rehearsals through December 2026, a September showcase, and an October 6 open house, so status is active. The site gives only per-event iCal links, so no full calendar feed is recorded. The email is the chorus address published on the audition page. The site does not name the nearest SEPTA stop; it lists bus routes 21, 42, 17 and 2 serving nearby stops.
